log: ARE THE PROPOSED CHANNELS EVEN VIABLE? -- annotation coverage, stratified by obscurity
Every proposed channel rests on an annotation, and annotation is what obscure genes lack.
A channel can show a real average lift while contributing nothing on the 9,186 gaps, which
are obscure by construction. This costs minutes and decides which channels are worth days.
prot_pfam: 8609 genes carry domains | tf_core: 9906 edges, 979 distinct targets, 940 distinct regulators
4771 distinct annotated catalyst genes in the benchmark's enzyme-shaped population
COVERAGE BY LITERATURE BIN (fraction of catalyst genes carrying the annotation)
READING -- the gate is the obscure column (0-20 papers), not the average.
pfam         obscure coverage 0.716  slope -0.162 (-0.52 of the ppi calibrator)   VIABLE, AND ANTI-CORRELATED WITH FAME -- better where the gaps are
tf_in        obscure coverage 0.000  slope +0.092 ( 0.30 of the ppi calibrator)   DEAD for this task: the annotation is absent where the gaps are

enh          obscure coverage 0.934  slope +0.034 ( 0.11 of the ppi calibrator)   VIABLE: present on obscure genes and not a fame proxy
ppi          obscure coverage 0.431  slope +0.310 ( 1.00 of the ppi calibrator)   DEAD for this task: the annotation is absent where the gaps are
Note on `ppi`: it is included as a CALIBRATOR, not a proposal. Interaction degree is the
textbook fame-driven annotation, so its slope is what a contaminated channel looks like on
this axis, and the others should be read against it rather than against zero.
